messages.subject: Shrinkage in MLMs
parts:
I would like to introduce shrinkage in an analysis investigating the effect of drug treatment on multiple  outcomes, each measured at multiple locations.

My general question is if (and how) this can be done in rstanarm. My data is completely crossed.

For example, when I have data with following columns:
y: normalized outcome values
ID: participant indicator 
Treatment: Drug or placebo indicator (each participant tested on both placebo and drug)
Outcome:  outcome type indicator
Location:  location indicator

potential model:

y ~ 1 + (1 | ID) + ( Treatment | Outcome / Location )


I would like to report the effects of Treatment on each Outcome at each Location. 
My question then is if the treatment effect will be estimated such that shrinkage occurs across the outcomes and across locations, and what are the random participant (ID) intercepts really doing in this model?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Shrinkage in MLMs
parts:
On Wednesday, April 13, 2016 at 10:08:22 AM UTC-4, Athanasia Monika Mowinckel wrote:

I would like to introduce shrinkage in an analysis investigating the effect of drug treatment on multiple  outcomes, each measured at multiple locations.

My general question is if (and how) this can be done in rstanarm. My data is completely crossed.
The rstanarm package doesn't do anything with simultaneous models of multiple outcomes at the moment, unless you stack the data like you do below. The brms package might.

For example, when I have data with following columns:
y: normalized outcome values
I wouldn't normalize the outcome(s) in advance. It is usually better to estimate on the raw data and normalize the posterior predictive distribution.

ID: participant indicator 
Treatment: Drug or placebo indicator (each participant tested on both placebo and drug)
Outcome:  outcome type indicator
Location:  location indicator

potential model:

y ~ 1 + (1 | ID) + ( Treatment | Outcome / Location )


I would like to report the effects of Treatment on each Outcome at each Location. 
My question then is if the treatment effect will be estimated such that shrinkage occurs across the outcomes and across locations, and what are the random participant (ID) intercepts really doing in this model?

I'm not sure I understand. If the subjects stay in the same location throughout, then wouldn't ID be nested within location but not within outcome?

Ben

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Shrinkage in MLMs
parts:
On Wednesday, April 13, 2016 at 10:50:37 AM UTC-4, Athanasia Monika Mowinckel wrote:
you say "The rstanarm package doesn't do anything with simultaneous models of multiple outcomes at the moment, unless you stack the data like you do below. The brms package might."
Do you mean that even though I stack my data like this, rstanarm cannot do what I want?

Hi Mo, I think Ben meant that the way you seem to have your data structured should work ok with rstanarm, we just haven't yet implemented a more general way of handling multiple outcome models. Also, if you're going to go with a formula like that I recommend updating to the current state of rstanarm on github (instructions in the readme file) as the posterior_predict function should now be able to handle models with those nested group formulas better than before. We'll also be releasing a CRAN update soon (hopefully quickly following the release of R 3.3.0 in < 2 weeks) if you want to wait for that, but the github version should be working now. 

Jonah

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Shrinkage in MLMs
parts:
Hi Mo,

I too have a hard time remembering and differentiating between all the lme4 formula options. It definitely gets confusing. In your original formula you have

(1|ID) + (Treatment | Outcome/Location)

which I think expands to / is equivalent to 

(1|ID) + (Treatment | Outcome) + (Treatment | Outcome:Location)

I think this syntax means that the intercept varies by participant and that treatment effect varies by outcome and by location within outcome.

Does that sound like the model you want to estimate?

Jonah

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Shrinkage in MLMs
parts:
The only other alternative is to reparameterize. You
want to look at your posterior and see where the divergences
are arising to see if that gives you a clue. Look to keep
the scales near 1 and the variables as uncorrelated as
possible in the posterior.

stepsize is just the initial stepsize. It then goes
through adaptation based on adapt_delta.

- Bob
